incident_management_disposition.bound: No selected J1 artifact declares incident-management as an active dependency. This is absence from the artifact-derived closure. It is not a finding that the package is globally extraneous, not proof of contamination, and not authorization to remove it from the historical snapshot or from any environment.

limitations: SHA-256 binds the bytes this task selected for V2. It does not establish that these are the bytes historically used in V1: the historical records carry name and version only, and no historical artifact identity exists to compare against.

The dependency closure was derived from the metadata inside the selected artifacts. That is present-day metadata for present-day artifacts; it is not proof of what was historically required, which remains the largest disclosed gap from PR #164.
An artifact-metadata closure cannot see a dependency reached only through a plugin registry, an entry point or a data-driven import.

No native library below the Python distribution level is pinned by any authority. torch, numpy, scipy and scikit-learn carry compiled extensions and soundfile binds libsndfile; the wheels vendor these, and no authority records their versions.

8 of the 47 external members have more than one tag-compatible wheel for their pinned version. A hash alone does not restrict which wheel pip attempts, so installation must be restricted to the approved bytes by mechanism, not by the hash line alone.
The base image is trusted by digest. It is not independently reproduced from source.
The clean-room qualification ran on a host kernel, not inside the authorized base image. Nothing in this task built or ran an OCI image.

An independent re-derivation of the J1 internal module closure for this task's import qualification reached 108 modules where PR #164's reached 113. The traversal rules differ; both reach the same six third-party import roots, and every module in the J1 package was reached by both. The difference was not investigated and #164 is not contradicted.
